Command: Do not eat a sin offering whose blood was brought into the sanctuary
Summary: The command: Do not eat a sin offering whose blood was brought into the sanctuary (Leviticus 6:30). A sin offering whose blood was carried into the holy place to make atonement was wholly burned, not eaten.
Commandment: Do not eat a sin offering whose blood was brought into the sanctuary.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: A sin offering whose blood was carried into the holy place was wholly burned, not eaten — a ceremonial law drawing a hard line. Its goal was to keep the most solemn atonement offerings entirely God's, untouched by any table. The evil was treating the deepest atonement as common food, eating what belonged wholly to the altar. It restrained that by burning the offering whole: where the blood went in, the flesh did not come out to be eaten.
